scope: Proposition 8.1 (Finite-order packets) of the manuscript “Smooth counterexamples to Yau's nodal upper bound in dimensions three and four” (preprints/Smooth-counterexamples-to-Yaus-nodal-upper-bound-in-dimensions-three-and-four-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 350 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8e4c129bdb0f2f45), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 40-41. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For any integers ℓ, J ≥ 0, and all sufficiently large integers k, there are packets indexed by Yk = (k−1 Z4 ) ∩ U3, y ∈ Yk, 1 ≤ j ≤ 3, of the form pyj,k(x) = ekΦyj(x) Ayj,k(x)ξ(x − y). (8.2) Here ξ is a smooth cutoff supported in a fixed small ball, equal to one in a smaller ball; all translated supporting balls lie in P. The phases are complex polynomials in x − y, and the amplitudes are polynomials of fixed finite degree in x − y and k−1. Their coefficients are uniformly bounded over the centers and indices. They satisfy Φyj(y) = f(y), dΦyj(y) = df(y) + ib♭ j, ℜ Hessh Φyj(y) = Hy − cyjhy, Ayj,k(y) = 1. (8.3) On each supporting ball, for positive constants c, C, −C|x − y|2 ≤ ℜΦyj(x) − f(x) ≤ −c|x − y|2 , Ayj,k(x) = 1 + O(|x − y| + k−1 ). (8.4) The amplitude and each of its fixed-order derivatives are uniformly bounded. For every fixed multi-index α, |∂α pyj,k(x)| ≤ Cαk|α| ekf(x)−ck|x−y|2 , (8.5) 40 after decreasing c if necessary, and sup x∈P e−kf(x) X |α|≤ℓ ∂α (∆h + Λk)pyj,k(x) ≤ Cℓ,J k−J . (8.6) The radii, coefficients, constants, and frequency threshold are fixed before k varies.
